methodology: Read canonical English Qur'an from existing production database and checked English biblical passage texts at linked locators. Not a critical original-language edition or manuscript audit. Source candidates are not verified or publishable; no literary dependence asserted.

records.note: Reversal after mercy and recording conspiracies; broad motifs, no sufficiently specific earlier text isolated.

candidates.similarity: A storm endangers a ship and sailors appeal to deity for deliverance.
candidates.difference: Jonah recounts a specific prophet, casting lots and casting him into the sea, followed by sacrifice and vows; 10:22 describes a generalized maritime danger and promise of gratitude, leading into a critique of subsequent wrongdoing in 10:23.
candidates.limitations: English KJV inspected; Hebrew critical text, witness history, composition and manuscript dates not independently verified.

records.note: Continuation of 10:22's storm example, contrasting rescue with renewed injustice. No separate precise earlier narrative association established.

candidates.similarity: Flourishing plant life rapidly vanishes, exemplifying the transience of mortal life.
candidates.difference: Psalm 90 depicts human life as morning grass withering by evening; 10:24 depicts rain-fed vegetation and a cultivated landscape suddenly devastated by divine command. Imagery and rhetorical framing differ.
candidates.limitations: English translations compared; Hebrew critical text and textual witnesses, historical setting and dating not independently verified.

records.note: Invitation to abode of peace and guidance; broad doctrinal language without distinctive pre-Islamic textual locus established.
